newsitem.title: USA: Tight money could force SPR oil sale - U.S. rep.
newsitem.headline: Tight money could force SPR oil sale - U.S. rep.

text.p: The chairman of a House Interior Appropriations subcommittee said Tuesday he wanted to avoid another oil sale from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), but said tight money could force a sale.
"If we don't get an increase in allocation, we're going to have another sale of SPRO oil," Rep. Ralph Regula, an Ohio Republican, said at a subcommittee hearing.
After the hearing, Regula said, "I'm going to do the best I can to avoid that," and said it will depend on how large an appropriation programs under his panel's jurisdiction get from budget writers.
"We've been opposing it, but we get caught in a numbers crunch. But at least the administration is opposing it this year," Regula told reporters.

Asked if he knew of alternatives to a sale from the oil reserve if the allocation is short, Regula said, "Not unless we have a good banker. Once we get the allocation we'll have to make policy choices. We'll have to prioritize."
Regula said he believed the Strategic Petroleum Reserve should be under the Defense Department's budget, instead of interior and energy programs.

He said would it would be easier to protect the reserve if it were part of the Defense Department's budget "because they have so much more money. If you have $200 million in the defense budget, they spill that every day."
At the hearing, Energy Secretary Federico Pena reiterated that he opposed additional sales from the petroleum reserve.
"Our goal and intention is not to have any more sales out of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve," Pena said.

The administration in its budget plan for 2002 proposed selling $1.1 billion worth of oil to help balance the budget, but Pena has said that is just a "place marker" and the administration would search for alternatives.

The Clinton administration first proposed selling some SPR oil to help pay to close one of the storage sites that had a potential to leak. Since then, there have been two more sales to raise money or to pay to run the SPR program.
Pena has said the reserve must be maintained at substantial levels to have market-calming effects in case of a supply disruption.
